discussion_comments.comment_body: please use gjson and sjson here to avoid parsing entire body
Done — switched to `gjson`/`sjson` in 9f7dc1f, no full-body unmarshal now. Added a leading-`{` guard since they do not validate JSON, so multipart bodies stay untouched.

I checked this against the actual library behaviour rather than assuming, and I'm going to skip `ValidBytes` — but the comment did surface something worth pinning, so thanks.

What `gjson` v1.18.0 / `sjson` v1.2.5 actually do:

| input | `gjson.GetBytes(_, "model")` | `sjson.SetBytes(_, "model", "DEP")` |
|---|---|---|
| `{"model":"a"} trailing` | `"a"` | `{"model":"DEP"} trailing` |
| `{"model":"a", "x":` | `"a"` | `{"model":"DEP", "x":` |
| multipart w/ `name="model"` | Null | **`{"model":"DEP"}`** |

On the valid-prefix-plus-trailing-data case the rewrite is faithful: it swaps the alias and leaves the malformed remainder malformed. Azure returns the same 400 parse error before and after, so `ValidBytes` buys no change in outcome — only a full O(n) scan of every passthrough body. That matters here specifically: the route this PR exists for is `/providers/mistral/azure/ocr`, whose bodies are base64-encoded PDFs, and the review ask on this line was to stop scanning the whole body.

The genuinely destructive row is the third one — on a non-JSON input `sjson.SetBytes` discards the body and returns a bare `{"model":"DEP"}`, which on `/audio/transcriptions` would throw away the uploaded file. That is already blocked twice over (leading-`{` guard, and `gjson` returns Null anyway), but it had no test. Added in 95dddec: the non-JSON subtest now uses a realistic multipart body with a `name="model"` form field carrying the alias, so the guard fails loudly if anyone relaxes it.

The `json.Unmarshal(gotBody, &...)` validation in `TestResolvePassthroughAlias` is untouched.

Addressed in [a9fd5cf](https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/pull/2054/commits/a9fd5cf5343ad585449c3d18a07fed3291c786d0).

The token exchange now runs on a dedicated `fasthttp.Client` with `MaxResponseBodySize: tokenExchangeMaxResponseBytes` (64 KiB) set at the transport layer, so the cap is enforced before the body is buffered — on both success and error paths.

- Dedicated client: `core/providers/copilot/copilot.go` lines 48–58
- Cap constant: `core/providers/copilot/utils.go` line 48
- Wired into the token-manager constructor: `core/providers/copilot/copilot.go` lines 96 and 106

this actually can be optimized using sonic.

use sonic here. specifically `sonic.Get(body, "model")`

https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/bytedance/sonic#Get

if the purpose here is to just read the model from incoming request and rewrite it with pure model you can use `gjson` and `sjson` to avoid parsing entire request.

```
body := string(ctx.PostBody())
model := gjson.Get(body,"model")
provider, model := schemas.ParseModeString(string(model), "")
sjson.Set(body,"model",model) 
```

and then you can Marshal it into PassthroughRequest using Sonic or manually (again if manual then use gson as that would avoid marshalling entire request)

Refactored in 801cd66 - switched to gjson/sjson for the model read-and-rewrite. Removed the `ResponsesCompactRequest` struct and the double unmarshal. The handler now reads the model with `gjson.Get`, rewrites it with `sjson.Set`, and deletes `fallbacks` with `sjson.Delete` - no full request parsing needed.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
No allocation happens here — `ChannelMessage` embeds `schemas.BifrostRequest` **by value**, so `msg.BifrostRequest = schemas.BifrostRequest{}` just zeroes the embedded struct's fields in place (a memset over memory the message already owns). Nothing new goes on the heap.

Pooling is also unaffected on the acquire side: `getChannelMessage` already does `msg.BifrostRequest = req` on every Get, which overwrites the same memory whether or not it was zeroed at release. What the pool saves — reusing the `ChannelMessage` object and its channels — is untouched.

The separately pooled `*schemas.BifrostRequest` (from `bifrostRequestPool`, released in the handle methods for fallbacks) is not touched by this line either; only the message's value copy is cleared, so its pointers (`ChatRequest` → full parsed body, etc.) stop pinning that memory while the message sits idle in the pool.

Net cost: one struct-sized zeroing per release. Net benefit: an idle pooled message no longer retains the last request's multi-MB body and context.

discussion_comments.comment_body: This is intentional and documented in the chFilterMissing comment. The tables are keyed (timestamp, id), so an id-only lookup falls back to ClickHouse's generic exclusion search (near-full scan of the id column - see https://clickhouse.com/docs/optimize/sparse-primary-indexes), while the timestamp bound enables primary-key granule pruning. It is safe because retried creates reuse the original entry (same timestamp) under the RMW locks, and the tables' dedup key is (timestamp, id) anyway - a same-id row at a different timestamp is a distinct logical row regardless of this check. An unbounded fallback for not-found ids would run the expensive scan on every genuinely new insert (the hot path), defeating the optimization.

+	gateFlusherCh   chan *schemas.BifrostStreamChunk // captured on first GateSend; reused by flusher
+	gateFlusherCtx  *schemas.BifrostContext          // captured on first GateSend
+	gateFlusherOn   bool                             // flusher goroutine running
+	gateFlusherDone chan struct{}                    // closed when the most recent flusher exits; nil when no flusher has ever started
+	// gatePendingCleanup is set by cleanupStreamAccumulator when the caller
+	// requested teardown but the gate is still busy (flusher running or
+	// Paused). The flusher's exit defer checks this flag and re-runs cleanup
+	// once the gate is idle, so teardown can't race ahead of the flusher.
+	gatePendingCleanup bool
+	parent             *Accumulator // back-reference for deferred cleanup re-entry
discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed — added a 100 MB hardcoded cap on the paused replay buffer (`gateReplayBufMaxBytes` in `framework/streaming/gate.go`). Tracking `gateReplayBufBytes` on `StreamAccumulator` (`types.go:160`); on overflow the gate transitions to `Ended` with a synthetic `paused_replay_buffer_overflow` BifrostError that the flusher delivers as the terminal chunk, so the consumer is notified and memory is released. Bytes counter resets to 0 on drain success / ctx-done abandon / forceEnd cleanup.
